title: Foundations of GenIR
extended_summary:
This chapter/paper provides a conceptual and technical foundation for generative AI in information retrieval and information access. It asks how modern generative models, especially large language models, change the design of information access systems and what new paradigms they enable. The paper does not evaluate an educational intervention; instead, it surveys model architecture, scaling, training, prompting, and multimodal capabilities as background for understanding generative information retrieval (GenIR).

The main approach discussed is twofold: information generation, where generative models directly create tailored outputs for user needs, and information synthesis, where models integrate external evidence to produce grounded responses. Within information synthesis, the paper reviews retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), modular retrieval strategies, retrieval planning for composite information needs, and related questions of reliability, hallucination mitigation, and multi-source information use. It also covers generative retrieval and domain-specific modeling as alternatives or complements to traditional retrieval pipelines.

Because the chapter is theoretical, there is no participant population, school setting, or intervention implementation context. Its conclusions are that generative AI can substantially enhance information access, but reliability, hallucination, grounding, controllability, and system design remain central challenges. The paper argues that future progress will depend on better integration of retrieval and generation, stronger methods for external knowledge use, and more transparent and controllable model-based information systems.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A general generative AI / large language model paradigm that produces human-like text and can also synthesize or integrate external information (e.g., via retrieval-augmented generation).
identified_tools.use_case: This chapter reviews foundational generative AI concepts, including information generation and information synthesis, with examples such as ChatGPT, Bing with retrieval-augmented generation, and multimodal generative systems; it is not an empirical study of a single tool.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/theoretical chapter about generative AI foundations and information access, not an empirical evaluation of an instructional-coaching or lesson-feedback tool. No study design, sample, or outcome evidence is reported.
impact_tier_rationale: The chapter is influential as background synthesis on generative AI and retrieval-augmented generation, but it reports no measured educational impact. Because no direct outcomes are evaluated, practical impact for the requested school coaching use case is not established.
